1

About 900 years

Slide 215.9 s, 7 beats7 points

Answers the deck’s question: “About what years does the medieval period cover?”

Beat 10.0–2.2 s

On screen476Western Roman Empire falls

Moves
Opens on a Roman column. A crack runs across it, the top half topples and lands beside the stump. A gold band (the medieval period) starts to roll out along the table from the year 500.
Camera
Long lens on the column, slow drift.
Sound
Stone creak, a heavy fall and rubble, then the band unrolling like a ribbon.

Beat 22.2–4.4 s

On screen800Charlemagne crowned emperor

Moves
The band runs on, to scale, and the camera follows it to a cushion. A crown drops onto it and settles with a glint.
Camera
Whips right along the band to the year 800.
Sound
Whoosh, a soft thump on velvet, a bright metal ring.

Beat 34.4–6.6 s

On screenc. 1025Guido’s staff notation

Moves
A sheet ruled with four lines. A quill sets six square notes on it, stepping upwards one at a time.
Camera
Whips right to c. 1025, a little higher to read the page.
Sound
Six pen strokes, each with a rising plucked note.

Beat 46.6–8.8 s

On screenc. 1200four-voice music in Paris

Moves
The twin towers of Notre Dame. Four notes in four colours pop up in a stack in front of it, one voice at a time.
Camera
Whips right to c. 1200, pulled back for the towers.
Sound
Four sung tones building a chord, with a bell.

Beat 58.8–11.0 s

On screen1360sMachaut’s Mass

Moves
A thick bound book lands on the table: a whole Mass by one composer.
Camera
Whips right to the 1360s.
Sound
A heavy book thud, a page rustle, one chord.

Beat 611.0–13.2 s

On screenc. 1400Renaissance begins

Moves
The gold band reaches its end. A sun rises behind the end post, rays flicking on twos.
Camera
A short whip right to the end of the band.
Sound
The ribbon stops with a tick; a warm rising tone and a ding.

Beat 713.2–15.9 s

On screenc. 500–1400about 900 years, between ancient Rome and the Renaissance

Moves
Everything hops together into one row over a short gold band: column, crown, staff, cathedral, book, sunrise. Holds.
Camera
Pulls back to hold the whole row for the last second and a half.
Sound
Six landings in a run, a paper slap for the caption, a last chord.

When was it? Tap the object for each date.

Graded check7 points

After the animationWhen was it? Tap the object for each date.

How
Six dates come up one at a time in shuffled order (476, 800, c. 1025, c. 1200, 1360s, c. 1400). Tap the object that marks each one. Then: "About what years does the medieval period cover?" with three choices.
Camera
Holds on this framing; the scene is live 3D, so taps land on the objects themselves.
Sound
A ding and the object’s own sound for a right answer, a low buzz for a wrong one.
2

Two worlds: church and court

Slide 311.7 s, 4 beats6 points

Answers the deck’s question: “What is the difference between sacred and secular music?”

Beat 10.0–2.6 s

On screenSACREDmusic for worship: prayer and church services

Moves
Opens on a chant book lying open on a lectern, a candle beside it. The flame flickers on threes.
Camera
Long lens, level with the book, drifting.
Sound
Room tone, one low held sung tone, a candle flutter.

Beat 22.6–5.2 s

On screenSACREDsung in Latin by monks, nuns, and choirs

Moves
A quill moves across the page and sets down square notes one by one. Every note stays where it is written.
Camera
Whips a little higher and closer to look down on the page.
Sound
Pen strokes on parchment, a sung tone for each note, all in step.

Beat 35.2–8.2 s

On screenSECULARmusic for everyday life: entertainment and dancing

Moves
The other end of the table: a lute hops in and strums. Notes fly up out of it and vanish in the air, one after another.
Camera
Fast whip right across the table.
Sound
Whoosh, a wooden tock, plucked lute notes in a dance rhythm, a small pop as each note vanishes.

Beat 48.2–11.7 s

On screenSACREDcarefully written downSECULARmostly passed on by ear

Moves
Both at once: on the left the notes sit safe in the book; on the right three juggling balls go round and the lute’s notes keep flying off and disappearing.
Camera
Pulls back to a wide two-shot and holds.
Sound
Held chant on the left, lute dance on the right, two paper slaps for the captions.

Sacred or secular? Tap the book or the lute for each clue.

Graded check6 points

After the animationSacred or secular? Tap the book or the lute for each clue.

How
Six clues from the slide, one at a time in shuffled order ("Latin", "entertainment and dancing", "monks, nuns, and choirs", "troubadours and minstrels", "prayer and church services", "local, everyday languages"). Tap the chant book for sacred or the lute for secular.
Camera
Holds on this framing; the scene is live 3D, so taps land on the objects themselves.
Sound
A ding and the object’s own sound for a right answer, a low buzz for a wrong one.
3

One melody, then many

Slides 4 and 611.7 s, 4 beats4 points

Answers the deck’s question: “Is Gregorian chant monophonic or polyphonic? How can you tell?”

Beat 10.0–2.8 s

On screenMONOPHONYchant, c. 500–900: one line for everyone

Moves
Opens on four monks in a row behind a long sheet of parchment. They bob together, mouths open, and ONE row of black square notes steps across the sheet as they sing. A black tag over each head shows they share the line.
Camera
Long lens from the front, slow drift.
Sound
One sung line in unison (stacked sine voices), no beat, a long church echo.

Beat 22.8–5.6 s

On screenORGANUMfrom c. 900: a second voice travels along with the chant

Moves
Two of the monks’ tags flip to red and a second, red row of notes appears just above the chant, moving in step with it.
Camera
Snaps to a slightly higher angle on the sheet.
Sound
The same line, now doubled a fifth above.

Beat 35.6–8.4 s

On screenNOTRE DAME, PARISc. 1160–1250: Léonin writes for 2 voices; Pérotin for 3 and 4

Moves
A third (gold) and a fourth (white) row arrive with busier shapes of their own. Every monk now has his own colour and they bob out of step.
Camera
Snaps round and pulls back a little to hold four rows.
Sound
Two quick upper voices dancing over the slow chant; a bell on the fourth voice.

Beat 48.4–11.7 s

On screenPOLYPHONYtwo or more different melodies at the same time

Moves
All four rows complete on the sheet, four colours, four shapes. The monks keep singing. Holds.
Camera
Settles square-on above the sheet and holds.
Sound
All four voices land on one open chord that rings out.

Look at the sheet and choose.

Graded check4 points

After the animationLook at the sheet and choose.

How
The sheet changes for each question. One row of notes: "This is Gregorian chant. Monophonic or polyphonic?" Four rows: "And this?" Two rows: "What is this early polyphony called?" Then: "Who wrote for 3 and 4 voices at Notre Dame?"
Camera
Holds on this framing; the scene is live 3D, so taps land on the objects themselves.
Sound
A ding and the object’s own sound for a right answer, a low buzz for a wrong one.
4

Plucked, bowed, cranked

Slides 9 and 1013.5 s, 5 beats5 points

Answers the deck’s question: “Name two medieval instruments. How does each one make its sound?”

Beat 10.0–2.6 s

On screenPLUCKEDharp: small enough to rest on the lap

Moves
Opens on a small harp. A quill plectrum steps from string to string; each pluck throws a tick mark and a round note.
Camera
Long lens on the harp, drifting.
Sound
Plucked notes rising up a scale, short and clear.

Beat 22.6–5.2 s

On screenBOWEDvielle: the medieval fiddle

Moves
A vielle. A bow slides back and forth across its strings on twos and a long wavy line of sound streams out.
Camera
Whips right to the vielle.
Sound
A sustained, reedy bowed tone that swells with each stroke.

Beat 35.2–7.8 s

On screenCRANKEDhurdy-gurdy: a crank turns a wheel that rubs the strings

Moves
A hurdy-gurdy lying on the table. Its crank goes round, the wheel spins and one unbroken line of sound comes out: the drone.
Camera
Whips right, higher, to look down at the wheel.
Sound
A buzzing drone that never stops, with a click on every turn of the crank.

Beat 47.8–10.4 s

On screenLOUDshawm, a double reed, and nakers, small kettledrums

Moves
A shawm standing on its bell and a pair of nakers. The sticks beat the drums in turn, the shawm blasts jagged lines and bolts, and both jump with every hit.
Camera
Whips right and back to take in both.
Sound
A piercing nasal blast and pounding kettledrums, much louder than anything before.

Beat 510.4–13.5 s

On screenSOFTlike most strings: played indoorsLOUDoutdoors and for dancing

Moves
All five hop into one row: the three strings together on the left, playing gently; the shawm and nakers on the right, still blasting. Holds.
Camera
Pulls back to hold the whole row.
Sound
Soft strings on the left, loud band on the right, two paper slaps for the captions.

How does it make its sound? Tap the instrument for each clue.

Five clues, one at a time in shuffled order ("plucked", "bowed: the medieval fiddle", "a crank turns a wheel that rubs the strings", "a double reed with a piercing sound", "a pair of small kettledrums"). Tap the instrument that fits.

Holds on this framing; the scene is live 3D, so taps land on the objects themselves.

Four composers to remember

Slide 1114.1 s, 5 beats4 points

Answers the deck’s question: “Which composer was an abbess? Which one wrote a complete Mass?”

Beat 10.0–2.8 s

On screenHILDEGARD OF BINGEN1098–1179, German abbesswrote more than 70 chants and a sung play

Moves
Opens on an abbess in a veil. Beside her, pages of chant drop one after another onto a pile that keeps growing.
Camera
Long lens on the figure and the pile, drifting.
Sound
One clear high sung line; a soft paper landing for every page.

Beat 22.8–5.6 s

On screenLÉONINactive late 1100s, Notre Dame, Paristwo-voice organum for the whole church year

Moves
A cleric with a sheet in front of him. Two rows of square notes, black and red, step across it together.
Camera
Whips right to Léonin.
Sound
Two sung lines moving together, pen strokes.

Beat 35.6–8.4 s

On screenPÉROTINactive c. 1200, Notre Dame, Parisexpanded organum to three and four voices

Moves
A second cleric. His sheet starts with two rows, then a third (gold) and a fourth (teal) row pop in above them.
Camera
Whips right to Pérotin.
Sound
The two lines again, then a third and a fourth voice stacking into a chord.

Beat 48.4–11.2 s

On screenGUILLAUME DE MACHAUTc. 1300–1377, French poet-composerthe Messe de Nostre Dame and many love songs

Moves
A poet in a soft hat. A thick book lands in front of him (the Mass) and two hearts pop up beside it (the love songs).
Camera
Whips right to Machaut.
Sound
A heavy book thud, a full chord, two light pops.

Beat 511.2–14.1 s

On screenHildegard of BingenLéoninPérotinGuillaume de Machautwe know these four because their names were written down

Moves
All four hop into one row with their objects. A name slip pops under each from left to right. Holds on the four.
Camera
Pulls back to hold the line-up.
Sound
Four paper slaps in a run, then one chord that rings out.

Who was it? Tap the composer for each clue.

Graded check4 points

After the animationWho was it? Tap the composer for each clue.

How
Four clues, one at a time in shuffled order ("a German abbess who wrote more than 70 chants", "wrote a complete Mass, the Messe de Nostre Dame", "two-voice organum for the whole church year", "expanded organum to three and four voices"). Tap the figure in the line-up of four.

What I assumed

  • ScopeAs with the 1950s deck, I used the slide faces, not the speaker notes, and built one experience for each of the five questions on the "Check your knowledge" slide, drawing on slides 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 10 and 11. Slides 5 (Guido of Arezzo), 7 (troubadours), 8 (four more genres), 12 (video list) and 13 (then and now) are not animated. Guido’s staff appears only as the c. 1025 stop on the timeline.
  • Scoring26 points in all, split as in the table above. The split and the tap-to-answer mechanics are my proposal. Wrong options in the multiple-choice questions come from elsewhere in the deck (estampie, motet, Machaut).
  • WordingCaptions are shortened or joined from the slide text: "music for worship: prayer and church services", "sung in Latin by monks, nuns, and choirs", "chant, c. 500–900: one line for everyone", "from c. 900: a second voice travels along with the chant", "shawm, a double reed, and nakers, small kettledrums", "like most strings: played indoors", "about 900 years, between ancient Rome and the Renaissance".
  • NumbersAll from the slides: 476, 800, c. 1025, c. 1200, 1360s, c. 1400; c. 500–1400 and "about 900 years"; chant alone c. 500–900, organum from c. 900, Notre Dame c. 1160–1250; the four composers’ dates. The timeline in experience 1 is drawn to scale (38 years to one unit) until the last beat, where everything closes up into one row that is not to scale.
  • PeoplePeople are shown as plain turned figures, like chess pawns, with a hood, veil, cap or hat and no portrait: monks for chant, an abbess for Hildegard, clerics for Léonin and Pérotin, a poet for Machaut. The deck shows manuscript pictures instead; say so if you would rather have objects only.
  • SymbolsA Roman column that breaks stands for 476; a crown on a cushion for 800; a four-line sheet with six stepping notes for Guido’s staff; a block model of Notre Dame’s west front for Paris; a bound book with a cross for the Mass; a rising sun for the Renaissance; hearts for Machaut’s love songs; three juggling balls for minstrels (juggling is on slide 7). Voices are rows of square notes in four colours.
  • InstrumentsFive of the eleven instruments are shown: harp, vielle, hurdy-gurdy, shawm and nakers. Lute, psaltery, bagpipe, recorder, portative organ and pipe and tabor are left out to keep the piece short. The models are simplified; the vielle stands upright so its strings and bow can be seen.
  • BuildFinal piece: one self-contained HTML file with five chapters, each with play/pause, scrub, time, sound toggle and loop, then its check and a score card at the end (name, mark per question, total out of 26). Plus one MP4 per chapter. Panels here are block-outs: secondary motion, sound and the checks come after your OK.

Three things to decide

  1. Is five the right set?I can add experiences for slide 5 (Guido makes music readable), slide 7 (troubadours), slide 8 (four more genres) or slide 13 (then and now), or drop any of these.
  2. Where should it go?Same score card as the 1950s set unless you say otherwise. Tell me the repository to push to (a new one, or a folder in johnshawler/50s); I will not push until you say.
  3. Any beat, caption or object to change?Name the experience and beat number. On your OK I build the full animations, sound and checks exactly as boarded here.
